original_card.acceptance_gate: Pin the current sources and one obligation; the historical owner audit is an example, not evidence of a current bug.

first_step.inspect: Read #2977 reported duplicate-scatter counterexample and its opt-in repair. The archive is not a production fix or an independently validated selected-result failure; the selected generator emits unique rows.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; does not replay or validate the reported bug.

original_card.first_experiment: First check whether the scatter repair has been adopted. If still open, independently reproduce #2977 symbolic-versus-exported parity on the tiny duplicate fixture, compare the selected unique-row positive control, and define either enforced uniqueness or consistent multiplicity semantics. A bounded guard-adoption patch must preserve valid inputs and test the actual exported action. Stop after this obligation; no full historical replay or frontier change follows from the mutant alone.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Closing a current acceptance gap or proof obligation strengthens reliability even without changing kappa.
allowed_variations: Audit one named current condition using a new semantic counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Reporting the historical timing-only diagnostic as a new current acceptance bug.
Calling a malformed mutant a failure of the selected construction, or importing an opt-in repair without testing the exporter boundary.

actual_scope: Answer #3696 OQ1 at the selected PR589 gate-operand boundary: on the pinned n=6, len(srcs)<=4 domain of the #3696 Sym/Exp lemma, compare the simple-support guard (all of d+srcs distinct) with the destination-absent guard (d not in srcs). Report whether each rejects all dest-in-sources divergent patterns without rejecting agreeing dest-free lists.
scope_change_reason: PR #3696 proved dest-free always agree and dest-in can diverge, and left OQ1 asking for a simple-support (or other) guard that rejects all divergent dest-in cases without rejecting agreeing dest-free lists. This package answers that guard-sharpness obligation; it does not reprint the #3696 dest_free_agree/selected_gates census as a new claim.
bottleneck_link: A successor schema needs to know whether scatter-style simple-support is sufficient for gate lists, or whether a weaker destination-absent check is the sharp guard that preserves all agreeing dest-free operand lists.
stop_rule: Stop after the two-guard census, named controls, and selected-word positive control. No production adoption, native replay, or kappa change. Do not modify research/gate-operand-export-parity/.
evidence: CERTIFICATE.json, PROOF.md, verify.py, independent.py and test_package.py. On n=6,len<=4: both guards reject all 3492 dest-in divergent patterns; dest-absent rejects 0 of 4686 agreeing dest-free lists; simple-support rejects 3450 agreeing dest-free lists (witness d=1,srcs=[0,0]). Predecessor tip 0581402f978addb2eda5306fd124001486c76b08.

open_questions.question: Should a successor opt-in exporter boundary adopt destination-absent (rather than full simple-support) for gate operand lists?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Destination-absent is the sharp answer to #3696 OQ1; simple-support would also block agreeing dest-free duplicate-source gates that Sym/Exp already treat as legal.
open_questions.first_step: Compose dest-absent with an existing opt-in checker/exporter wrapper and replay selected artifacts that currently use distinct operands only.
open_questions.blocked_by: Maintainer schema adoption; frozen exporters stay unchanged in this package.

open_questions.why_it_matters: Guard sharpness is orthogonal to whether the checker's present reject set already covers every dest-in divergent mutant that can appear on the selected word.
open_questions.first_step: Enumerate dest-in mutants of B[0] (and optionally other sections) under the pinned word and classify Sym/Exp disagreement versus checker reject.
open_questions.blocked_by: Left as #3696 OQ2; not answered here.
